abertura: Four people are on the call. One minute to say who you are, and then it is an open conversation.
Mark the three sentences that are true.

itens.t: Nobody will call your name.
itens.porque: Yes. In an online meeting, the person who speaks is the person who decides to speak.

itens.t: You should wait until someone asks you to speak.
itens.porque: No. If you wait, the hour ends and you did not say anything.

itens.t: Four sentences are enough to introduce yourself.
itens.porque: Yes. Name, place, what you do, and what is new this year. That is all.

itens.t: You need to explain your whole job title.
itens.porque: No. Nobody in another country knows what your job title means. Say what you DO.

itens.t: A question after your answer keeps you in the conversation.
itens.porque: Yes. Your answer ends, and your question opens the next turn.

itens.t: If you do not understand, it is better to say nothing.
itens.porque: No. Saying “can you repeat?” is normal. Saying nothing is what keeps you out.

sec1.rationale: Coming in is a decision, not an invitation. Four sentences and one question is everything a first appearance needs -- and it is what everyone else in that room is doing too.

nota.texto: Tudo das três aulas anteriores chega aqui junto: contar (aula 9), pedir de novo (aula 10) e perguntar (aula 11). Nada novo entra hoje.

sec1.pt: Quatro pessoas estão na chamada. Um minuto para dizer quem você é, e depois a conversa fica aberta. Marque as três frases verdadeiras.

doc.texto:
Marta -- teacher, Chile. Works with teacher training in twelve schools. It is her first time in this group.
Paulo -- coordinator, Portugal. A public school with nine hundred students. Works with families and data protection.
Sofia -- researcher, Mexico. Studies how teachers learn to use new tools. She has been in the group for two years.
You -- and nobody is going to say your name.

abertura: Who is the best person for each question?

itens.t: "How do teachers learn to use a new tool?"
itens.porque: Sofia. She has been in the group for two years, so she knows how teachers there learn.

itens.t: "How do you talk to families about data protection?"
itens.porque: Paulo. Data protection is his work this year.

itens.t: "Is this your first time here too?"
itens.porque: Marta. She said it is her first time, and so is yours — that is the thing you have in common.

itens.t: "How many schools do you work with?"
itens.porque: Marta. Twelve schools is her number.

itens.t: "What changed in the group in two years?"
itens.porque: Sofia. Two years in the group means she saw the change.

itens.t: "How many students are there in your school?"
itens.porque: Paulo. Nine hundred students, in his school.

nota.titulo: A pergunta certa para a pessoa certa
nota.texto: Todas as seis são boas perguntas. O que muda é a quem se pergunta — e perguntar à pessoa errada é a forma mais rápida de a conversa não ir a lugar nenhum.

sec2.pt: Você vê quem está na chamada e o que cada pessoa faz. Diga a quem você faria cada pergunta.

abertura: This is a complete introduction for a meeting like this one:

callout.texto: “Hi, my name is Joice. I am from São Paulo, in Brazil. I work with teacher training, and I am also a school director. This year I am working with AI in schools.”

abertura: Mark the three things this introduction does.

itens.t: It says what she does, not her job title.
itens.porque: Yes. I work with teacher training — four words, and everyone understands.

itens.t: It explains her doctorate.
itens.porque: No. There is no doctorate in it, and there does not need to be.

itens.t: It says something that is new this year.
itens.porque: Yes. This year… is the part that makes people ask a question.

itens.t: It says how long she has worked.
itens.porque: No. She does not say how long. In a first meeting nobody needs it.

itens.t: It gives the other people something to ask about.
itens.porque: Yes. That is what the last sentence is for.

itens.t: It apologizes for her English.
itens.porque: No. She does not apologize. You do not need to.

sec3.rationale: Four sentences, and the one about this year is the useful one: it hands the room a subject. An introduction that says everything leaves nobody with a question.

nota.texto: É a frase mais comum e a que mais custa: ela diz à sala que se preocupe com a sua língua em vez de ouvir o que você faz. Ninguém naquela sala fala inglês perfeito.

sec3.pt: Esta é uma apresentação completa para uma reunião como essa. Marque as três coisas que ela faz.

sec4.titulo: The question you did not expect
abertura: One of the three keeps you in the conversation.

itens.t: You did not understand the question.
alts: Sorry, I did not understand. Can you say it again?
I do not speak English very well.
itens.ok: Sorry, I did not understand. Can you say it again?

itens.t: You understood, but not one word in the middle.
You know part of the answer.
alts: In my school, we do it like this. I do not know about other schools.
itens.ok: In my school, we do it like this. I do not know about other schools.

itens.t: You answered, and now there is silence.
alts: And in your country? How does it work?
itens.ok: And in your country? How does it work?

itens.t: They asked two things and you answered one.
alts: And about the second part -- can I answer that too?
itens.ok: And about the second part -- can I answer that too?

nota.texto: Uma diretora de escola faz as cinco todo dia, em português, sem pensar. O que é novo é que elas têm de sair em outra língua, na velocidade da pergunta — e por isso estão escritas aqui antes.

sec4.pt: Uma das três perguntas mantém você dentro da conversa. Escolha qual.

nota.titulo: Seis frases, e nenhuma pede desculpa
nota.texto: Can I ask you something? parece pedir licença. Não pede: anuncia. Entre anunciar e pedir permissão está a diferença entre estar na conversa e assistir a ela.

sec5.pt: Escolha o sentido certo para cada expressão.

cl12.prompt: Three of these keep you in the conversation. Which three?

itens.t: "Sorry, I did not understand. Can you say it again?"
itens.porque: Yes. It says what you missed, and it asks for one thing.

itens.t: "I do not speak English very well."
itens.porque: No. It is about your English, and the meeting is not about your English.

itens.t: "In my school, we do it like this. I do not know about other schools."
itens.porque: Yes. You say what you know, and you say where it stops. That is an honest answer.

itens.t: "That is a difficult question."
itens.porque: No. It says nothing, and the person still waits for your answer.

itens.t: "And in your country? How does it work?"
itens.porque: Yes. You answer, and then you give the turn back with a question.

cl12.rationale: The three that work all do something: they ask, they answer what is known, or they hand the turn back. The two that do not just close the door politely.
